rows.text: Hashaton reanimates without using the graveyard. Discard a creature card, pay {2}{U}, and you get a tapped 4/4 black Zombie copy of it — so the enters-the-battlefield trigger fires, the body is always a 4/4 no matter what you discarded, and none of it depends on the card surviving in your yard. Five mana total for any creature in your deck, every turn, and at instant speed if your discard outlet is.

rows.name: Hashaton, Scarab's Fist
rows.text: two mana, and every creature card you discard becomes a 4/4 Zombie token copy for {2}{U}. It triggers on the DISCARD, not on the graveyard, which is why this deck plays through Rest in Peace far better than a normal reanimator deck.

rows.name: Bard, King of Dale
rows.text: token doubling. Every Hashaton activation makes TWO copies, which means two Archon of Cruelty triggers, two Angel of the Ruins triggers, two Gray Merchants. It also doubles your draws.

rows.name: The Scarab God
rows.text: the same effect from graveyards, including theirs, plus a drain and a scry each upkeep scaling with your Zombie count — and every Hashaton token is a Zombie.

rows.name: Gleaming Overseer
rows.text: your Zombie tokens get hexproof and menace. That covers every single thing Hashaton makes.

guide.title: Discard outlets, which are the real cost

rows.text: Hashaton needs a way to discard on demand. The outlets are the deck's engine; the fatties are interchangeable.

rows.name: Psychic Frog
rows.text: free, repeatable, and each discard grows it. Also draws on connection.

rows.name: Putrid Imp
rows.text: one mana, unlimited discards, from turn one.

rows.name: Likeness Looter
rows.text: loots every turn AND turns into a copy of anything in your graveyard.

rows.name: Rona, Herald of Invasion
rows.text: loots, untaps on every legendary spell, and flips into a 5/5 that strips their hand.

rows.name: Kitsa, Otterball Elite
rows.text: loots, and later copies your instants and sorceries.

rows.name: Ledger Shredder
rows.text: connives on everyone's second spell each turn, so it discards on their turns too.

rows.name: Raffine, Scheming Seer
rows.text: connive X where X is your attacker count. On a wide attack that discards three or four creature cards at once, and each one is a separate Hashaton trigger.

rows.name: Frantic Search
rows.text: free, discards two, and untaps three lands to pay for the Zombies.

rows.name: Monument to Endurance
rows.text: every discard becomes a card, a Treasure or three life from each opponent.

rows.name: Archfiend of Ifnir
rows.text: cycling means it discards itself, and every other discard puts a -1/-1 counter on each of their creatures.

rows.name: Angel of the Ruins
rows.text: plainscycling turns it into a land when you need one, and the cycling IS a discard, so you can Zombie it in the same motion.

rows.name: Ghostly Pilferer
rows.text: discards to become unblockable, and draws off untaps and off their graveyard casts.

guide.title: What you want to be discarding

rows.name: Archon of Cruelty
rows.text: the best target in the deck. The token's enter trigger makes an opponent sacrifice, discard and lose three, while you draw and gain — and it triggers again every time the Zombie attacks.

rows.name: Serra's Emissary
rows.text: name creature or instant. You and your whole board get protection from that card type, which is a hard lock against most decks.

rows.name: Consecrated Sphinx
rows.text: two cards for every card any opponent draws.

rows.name: Sphinx of the Second Sun
rows.text: an extra beginning phase every turn — another untap, another upkeep, another draw, and another Scarab God drain.

rows.name: Archfiend of Despair
rows.text: they cannot gain life, and every point they lost this turn is dealt again at end step. It doubles every drain in the deck.

rows.name: Angel of the Ruins
rows.text: two artifacts or enchantments exiled per copy.

rows.name: Ori, Plate Stacker
rows.text: destroys ALL artifacts and enchantments your opponents control. Doubled by Bard, it is a full reset of the table's noncreature permanents.

rows.name: Gray Merchant of Asphodel
rows.text: your devotion is high and the token copies count too.

rows.name: Riptide Gearhulk
rows.text: buries a nonland permanent from every opponent three cards deep in their library.

rows.name: Solitude
rows.text: free removal from hand, and a Zombie copy of it exiles another creature.

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: one mana, any graveyard.

rows.name: Animate Dead
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Necromancy
rows.text: flash it in at the end of their turn, or at instant speed to reanimate in response to a wrath.

rows.name: Phyrexian Reclamation
rows.text: buys a creature back to hand for two mana and two life — and back in hand means it can be discarded again.

rows.name: Likeness Looter
rows.text: becomes a copy of the best thing in the yard, permanently.

rows.name: Phyrexian Metamorph
rows.text: a copy of any creature or artifact on the battlefield, including theirs.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: one mana, exile, unconditional.

rows.name: Solitude
rows.text: free at instant speed.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Damn
rows.text: a two-mana removal spell early or a wrath late.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counter their wrath and spend the mana making two Zombies.

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: free protection on their turn for your combo turn.

rows.name: Dovin's Veto
rows.text: uncounterable.

rows.name: Swan Song
rows.text: one mana for a wrath or a removal spell.

rows.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse
rows.text: the same, for anything noncreature.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: overloaded, it clears the way for a board of 4/4 Zombies.

rows.name: March of Swirling Mist
rows.text: phases your board out of a wrath, or phases their blockers out of the way.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: usually free with a wide board, and it saves everything.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: nobody interacts on your turn, which is when the whole deck happens.

rows.name: Soul-Guide Lantern
rows.text: graveyard hate that costs you nothing, since Hashaton does not need your yard.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the best card in the deck on turns one through four.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: the Treasures pay the {2}{U} on Hashaton over and over.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn.

rows.name: Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff
rows.text: a Treasure every time anyone casts their second spell — which in a four-player pod is several a round.

rows.name: The Queen of Dale
rows.text: a loot AND a Soldier every time an opponent casts their first noncreature spell. It is a discard outlet that other people activate for you.

rows.name: Consecrated Sphinx
rows.text: the ceiling, whether cast or Zombified.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a discard outlet. Hashaton without one does nothing at all — Putrid Imp, Psychic Frog or Likeness Looter in the opener is worth more than any fatty in the deck.
Count to five, not three. A Hashaton turn costs {2}{U} on top of the outlet, so plan the turn where you have the discard, the mana, and a fatty in hand all at once.

rows.name: Bard, King of Dale
rows.text: this is the card that turns a good turn into a game-ending one. Prioritise finding it once the outlet is online.

rows.name: Archon of Cruelty
rows.text: discard it, do not cast it. Nine mana is unreachable; five mana for a 4/4 that triggers on entry and on every attack is the whole point of the deck.
